system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt: In the space below, draw an angle that is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw two rays (line segments) that meet at a single common endpoint, the vertex. Place the vertex at the bottom left of the space, draw one ray going straight to the right (horizontal), and draw the second ray from the same vertex going up and to the left so that the opening between the two rays is wider than a right angle (a square corner) but less than a straight line. For example, the second ray should point up and to the left at roughly 120 degrees from the first ray. Label the vertex, and optionally mark the angle with a curved arc between the two rays. This is an obtuse angle, between 90 and 180 degrees.
